title: Prospective randomized multicenter study on the use of a fibroblast matrix for soft tissue augmentation of the nasal dorsum
summary: Patients with very thin skin over the nasal dorsum may develop visible irregularities or discomfort after rhinoplasty. The aim of this study is to investigate a collagen matrix (Fibro-Gide) intended to strengthen soft tissue in this region. Participants are randomly assigned to one of two groups and followed for up to twelve months. In addition to ultrasound measurements, questionnaires regarding satisfaction and postoperative symptoms are collected.

interventions.name: Patients in the intervention group undergo rhinoplasty according to current standards with additional implantation of an individually tailored collagen matrix (Fibro-Gide) for soft tissue augmentation of the nasal dorsum.  Before surgery, soft tissue thickness is assessed using high-frequency ultras

The control group undergoes standard rhinoplasty without Fibro-Gide implantation.
Before surgery, soft tissue thickness is assessed using high-frequency ultrasound at eight predefined measurement points. Follow-up examinations are performed after 7 days, 6 weeks, 12 weeks, 6 months, and 12 months.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
ii. Ability to provide informed consent
iii. Patients have signed the informed consent form for participation in the study
iv. Primary or secondary rhinoplasty with clinically and sonographically thin soft tissue coverage (≤ 4 mm). This threshold may be exceeded if, despite a thicker soft tissue layer, the underlying nasal framework is clearly visible and there is a clinical indication for soft tissue augmentation of the nasal dorsum.
v. Patients agree and are able to comply with all study-related requirements, including attendance at follow-up visits
Exclusion criteria:
i. Immunosuppression
ii. Congenital coagulation disorders
iii. Inability to provide informed consent
